title: Ukrainians are not fighting for Zelenskyy. They are fighting for national survival.
gist: Peter Dickinson argues that Trump, Musk and the Kremlin are converging on a push to replace Zelenskyy, but this misreads Ukrainian motivation: Ukrainians fight for national survival against a Russia they see as genocidal, so a leadership change would not yield a Russia-friendly peace.

insights.claim: President Trump has renewed calls for new Ukrainian leadership, saying it is time for someone else to negotiate for Ukraine, after Zelenskyy criticized Trump's decision to ease sanctions pressure on Russia.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Easing of Russia sanctions plus US pressure on Kyiv's leadership raises the risk of a US-brokered settlement on Russian terms.
insights.quote: “I think it’s time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine,”

insights.claim: Trump's rhetoric against Zelenskyy mirrors the Kremlin's: Peskov said Russia is in complete agreement with Trump, and Lavrov said Zelenskyy has no desire to reach an agreement.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Rhetorical convergence between Washington and Moscow signals diplomatic pressure falling mainly on Kyiv.
insights.locator: The US President’s attacks on Zelenskyy closely mirror

insights.claim: Elon Musk and other prominent Trump supporters have backed the hardening US stance, with Musk writing on October 15 that it is time for Zelenskyy to go.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: The anti-Zelenskyy line has broad support within Trump's political coalition, making it durable policy rather than a passing remark.
insights.locator: Many of Trump’s most prominent supporters

themes.theme: Zelenskyy as an obstacle to peace: the counter-case

insights.claim: Zelenskyy has accepted every American ceasefire proposal, which Moscow rejected, and has offered territorial concessions that would leave Russia controlling almost a quarter of Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Undercuts the premise that Kyiv's leadership is the blocker; negotiating failure sits with Moscow.
insights.locator: It is not difficult to debunk portrayals

insights.claim: Putin has repeatedly declined Zelenskyy's offers of a face-to-face meeting, while questioning Zelenskyy's legitimacy because of the absence of wartime elections.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Legitimacy arguments give Moscow a standing pretext to reject any signed deal.
insights.quote: “You can negotiate with anyone, but because of his illegitimacy, Zelenskyy has no right to sign anything,”

insights.claim: Recent polling shows strong Ukrainian public support for Zelenskyy, who would very likely win a wartime election.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Removing him by pressure would lack domestic basis, so a replacement lacks a mandate for concessions.
insights.locator: Recent polling indicates strong Ukrainian public support

themes.theme: Ukrainian resolve rooted in survival, not personality

insights.claim: Replacing Zelenskyy would not produce a Russia-friendly peace, because no successor could realistically obtain a mandate to make peace on Russian terms; Ukrainian opposition centers on deals lacking long-term security guarantees.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Peace-deal scenarios premised on a Kyiv leadership change should be discounted.
insights.quote: This is delusional. Ukrainians are not fighting for Volodymyr Zelenskyy. They are fighting for national survival.

insights.claim: Most Ukrainians favor some negotiated settlement but strongly oppose any deal that fails to provide long-term security or sets the stage for further Russian aggression.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Any settlement lacking security guarantees faces domestic rejection in Ukraine, limiting what Kyiv can sign.
insights.locator: While most Ukrainians favor a negotiated settlement

insights.claim: Ukrainians view the war as existential and regard Western talk of limited Russian territorial ambitions as naive, taking for granted that the Kremlin's goal is a Ukraine without Ukrainians.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Explains why territorial-concession frameworks keep failing to end the war.

insights.claim: Ukraine's much-hyped resilience is driven largely by ordinary people's recognition of Russia's genocidal intentions, not by special endurance, even though most are exhausted after almost five years of war.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Resilience is conditional on perceived existential threat; it will persist as long as Russian aims appear unchanged.
insights.locator: This understanding of Russia’s genocidal intentions

themes.theme: Russian occupation as evidence of intent

insights.claim: Putin has long denied Ukrainian separateness, published a 5,000-word history essay before the full-scale invasion, describes occupied regions as historically Russian lands and boasted last year that all of Ukraine is ours.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Stated maximalist aims suggest limited-concession deals will not satisfy Moscow.
insights.locator: Ukrainians have reached this chilling conclusion

insights.claim: Freedom House has ranked Russian-occupied Ukraine as the least free place on earth for the past two years, and UN officials classified mass arrests of Ukrainian civilians in occupied regions as a crime against humanity.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Documented occupation conduct reinforces Ukrainian refusal to cede territory and strengthens the case for continued Western support.
insights.locator: Putin’s obsession with the destruction of Ukraine

insights.claim: Twenty percent of Ukraine is subject to national identity erasure that may qualify as genocide, and Ukrainians assume the remaining 80 percent would face the same if Russia installed a puppet regime in Kyiv.
insights.speaker: Peter Dickinson
insights.so_what: Fear of occupation-style treatment sets a hard floor under Ukrainian willingness to compromise.
insights.locator: Ukrainians know what is happening in the occupied territories
